Eli: Heads-up — saw a p99 jump on ded-prod around 2671234500, looks correlated with a spike in kernel fallthroughs to CUTLASS. attaching a tiny log snippet.
Maya: can you paste the profiler trace + the request shape? shortseq vs longseq matters here usually.
Eli: profiler snippet:
```
2026-03-17T18:02:12Z kernel_router: chosen=triton fallback=cutlass reason=mem_estimate>threshold seqlen=16 batch=1 kv_cache_hit=false
2026-03-17T18:02:12Z exec: launched cutlass path p99_ms=62
2026-03-17T18:02:12Z exec: triton_estimated_ms=18
```
Eli: request shape was typical PLG burst: many short seq <32, but a handful with seqlen=256 in same window. KV warmup was noisy — lots of cache misses.
Jonas: interesting — so router thought memory risk due to kv-prefetch? We recently toggled `kv_prefetch_enabled=true` in autoscale group B, right?
Priya: yes on group B. That prefetch can spike peak memory when KV misses stack. If the router's mem_estimator is conservative it will prefer CUTLASS which has smaller transient buf, but much slower latency for shortseq because it doesn't use the optimized attention kernel.
Maya: +1. Also saw an autotune change last night: commit 7f2c9d9 adjusted probe cadence from 50ms->200ms to reduce jitter. That can make the router stale and over-react when seqlen distribution shifts quickly.
Eli: repro command I used (one-liner):
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":8}' https://api.redwood.test/generate &
done
```
Eli: when I inject a few longseq requests mid-burst the router flips to CUTLASS and we p99 tripples.
Jonas: mitigation options:
- disable kv_prefetch for group B temporarily
- reduce mem_estimator sensitivity (increase hysteresis)
- shorten probe cadence for this pool
- add a rule: if seqlen_percentile(95) < 64 prefer triton unless hard OOM
Priya: I can push a quick canary: set `kv_prefetch_enabled=false` and `kernel_probe_window_ms=80` for pool-b and monitor 30m.
Maya: let's also capture a flamegraph and KV cache occupancy trace during canary — need to confirm whether prefetch was the real amplifier.
Eli: infra-bot: can you create a canary config PR and tag @Priya @Jonas ?
infra-bot: Created canary config branch `canary/pool-b-kv-prefetch-off` — PR #4821, applied to pool-b canary nodes (n=3). Monitoring channel: #infra-canaries.
Jonas: after canary flip, observed immediate drop in kernel fallthrough events (see metric `runtime.kernel.fallthrough.count` down 87%). p95 & p99 normalized within 10 minutes.
Maya: great. Still want a long-term fix: adjust autotune probe logic to be sequence-distribution aware and tie probe windows to recent seqlen-variance.
Priya: Agreed. I'll open a follow-up RFC: proposal to add `seqlen_window_percentiles` into the router decision and to include a lightweight sampler that marks requests with KV-miss tags.
Eli: action items:
- Priya: RFC + rough API changes (due EOD tomorrow)
- Jonas: rollback autotune probe change or make it conditional if kv_prefetch=true (short term)
- Maya: perf postmortem notes and sample traces (I can write)
- infra-bot: keep canary running 2h and then expand to 10 nodes if stable
Eli: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Priya: also noting for postmortem — we should avoid global probe cadence changes without pool-specific overrides.
Maya: agreed. closing loop once RFC and canary results in channel.
